rektion: sich vor etw./jdm. (Dat.) fürchten; etw./jdn. (Akk.) fürchten; ich fürchte, (dass) …
meaning_en: to fear, to be afraid (of); ich fürchte: I'm afraid (that)
definition_de: Angst vor etwas haben (sich vor Hunden fürchten); höflich: ich fürchte, … = leider glaube ich, … (Ich fürchte, wir haben den letzten Bus verpasst.)
example_de: Der kleine Junge fürchtet sich vor dem Gewitter und versteckt sich unter seiner Decke.
example_en: The little boy is afraid of the thunderstorm and hides under his blanket.
visual_idea: Collocation 'sich vor dem Gewitter fürchten': a small boy in bed with the blanket pulled up to his wide, frightened eyes while lightning flashes in the window. Fear is shown through body language plus a clear cause, and the picture teaches the pattern 'sich fürchten vor + Dat.'. Junge, Gewitter and Decke are visible. The polite 'ich fürchte, …' is in definition_de; it has no picture of its own.
image_prompt: a small boy of about five sits up in his bed in a dark children's room, the blanket pulled up to just under his wide frightened eyes, both hands clutching the edge of the blanket, a worn teddy bear pressed against him, behind the bed a window with a bright jagged lightning bolt in a dark stormy sky, rain on the glass, cold blue flash light on his face
negative_prompt: text, letters, watermark, signature, caption, blurry, extra fingers, deformed hands, cluttered background, multiple panels
video_prompt: a small boy sits in bed in a dark room, lightning flashes bright in the window behind him, he flinches, squeezes his teddy bear and pulls the blanket up over his head; static medium shot, rain running down the window
